statement: Define F(c), for a cell c with grid value not 2, as the least t >= 0 such that fire can reach c in t minutes from some cell of value 1, moving through adjacent cells of value not 2; if fire never reaches c, set F(c) = infinity. Call an integer w >= 0 feasible when there exist L >= 1 and cells p_0,...,p_L such that p_0=(0,0), p_L=(m-1,n-1), every p_k has grid value 0, p_k is adjacent (north, east, south, or west) to p_{k-1} for 1 <= k <= L, w < F(p_0), w+k < F(p_k) for every 1 <= k < L, and w+L <= F(p_L). Then maximum_minutes(grid) returns r such that: r = -1 if no w >= 0 is feasible; r = 1000000000 if every w >= 0 is feasible; otherwise r is the maximum feasible w, so r >= 0, r is feasible, and no w > r is feasible.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). The grid is rectangular: every row grid[i] has length n. 2 <= m,n <= 300, 4 <= m*n <= 20000. For every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is 0, 1, or 2. grid[0][0] = 0 and grid[m-1][n-1] = 0.

statement: The function maximum_minutes(grid) returns a result r; it does not fail with overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). The grid is rectangular: every row grid[i] has length n. 2 <= m,n <= 300, 4 <= m*n <= 20000. For every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is 0, 1, or 2. grid[0][0] = 0 and grid[m-1][n-1] = 0.

statement: Whenever maximum_minutes(grid) returns r, either r = -1 or 0 <= r <= 1000000000.

statement: Using the feasible-wait definition from spec_1, if r >= 0, then every integer w with 0 <= w <= r is feasible.

statement: With F defined as in spec_1, if F(0,0) is finite and maximum_minutes(grid) returns r, then r <= F(0,0) - 1. In particular, r is not 1000000000 in this case.
